claims.text: Mild pre-annealing induces Cu segregation to the surfaces of FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles.
Cu surface segregation lowers the local barrier to melting.
Melting begins through formation of a liquid surface shell that subsequently progresses into the particle.
The starting nanoparticles are solid before entering the premelting and melting regime.
The starting nanoparticles are compositionally homogeneous.
The starting nanoparticles have a narrowly controlled size distribution.
Rapid quenching suppresses Cu segregation relative to mild pre-annealing.
The comparison is performed under high vacuum at a controlled heating rate of 10–20 °C/min and with identical nanoparticle sizes.
A Cu-enriched surface layer acts as a nucleation site for premelting.
Cu preferentially migrates to the nanoparticle surface during mild pre-annealing.
Preferential Cu migration is caused by Cu's lower melting point.
Preferential Cu migration is caused by Cu's higher surface mobility.
Cu enrichment locally reduces the melting temperature at the nanoparticle surface.
Cu-enriched surfaces premelt before the nanoparticle cores.
The resulting liquid shell progressively invades the particle core.
Pre-annealed nanoparticles will begin surface melting at a lower temperature than rapidly quenched nanoparticles.
In-situ TEM will reveal liquid-shell formation in the pre-annealed nanoparticles.
Earlier melting will correlate with lower-temperature exothermic DSC signals.
EDX mapping will show a higher surface Cu concentration in pre-annealed particles.
DSC will measure endothermic onset temperatures corresponding to melting events.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome associates melting with exothermic DSC signals, whereas the measurement plan correctly characterizes the melting events as endothermic. The expected DSC signature is therefore internally inconsistent.
